text:
maya: Heads up — hitting steady memory growth on staging when running long streaming chats that do repeated tool calls (tool-loop). RSS climbs ~30% over ~2h and doesn’t go down after sessions end. Repro and profiles below.

liam: Can you drop the pmap/jemalloc stats and how you repro?

maya: Yep — quick snapshot from the failing run: 

```
pmap 314159
 total kB
  1024K r-xp  00000000 00:00 0   /app/bin/inference
 2100000K rw-p  00000000 00:00 0   [ anon ]
RSS: 2.1G

jemalloc stats (unstable):
allocated: 1.9G
active: 2.2G
mapped: 2.8G

heaptrack summary: hot regions in kv_cache::slot_table and slab-allocator (80% dominated by page metadata)
```

jonathan: I put the --kv-debug=pagewalk logs from the same run into gist, but pasted a couple lines here: 

```
KV_PAGE id=0x7f9b2a4f refcnt=3 pinned_by=session:abcd slot=5823 last_access=2026-02-11T12:04:33Z
KV_PAGE id=0x7f9b2a8c refcnt=3 pinned_by=tool-output:tool_x pending=true

pagewalk: page 0x7f9b2a8c still referenced after session close
```

girish: This smells like a regression from the adaptive batching heuristics we merged last week (commit abc1234). That change changed sequence-length clustering which increases prefix-sharing and can keep more KV pages live. Also changed kernel selection scheduling which shifted eviction timing. Two quick hypotheses: (1) more long-lived prefixes => real increased residency; (2) refcount leak on tool completion path.

hannah: I wrote a tiny repro: stream a 50-turn chat and in each turn call two tools in a tight loop (shelling out simulated tools). Repro script (very trimmed):

```
for i in range(1000):
  msg = client.stream_chat(session_id)
  for t in tools:
    resp = client.call_tool(t, payload)
    client.append_tool_output(session_id, resp)
  sleep(0.1)
```

Running that for ~90m reproduces the growth reliably on staging.

maya: I also toggled jemalloc background thread and decay params. With background_thread:true the growth is slightly delayed but still ends up similar. MALLOC_CONF used: 

```
MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:30000,muzzy_decay_ms:30000
```

perf-bot: Attached perf trace to the thread: https://perf.internal/runs/99231 (the trace shows repeated pagewalks and GC-like scans with growing live_set). :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

ops-bot: Alert fired for stg-inference-01 at 2026-02-11T12:10Z — memory > 85% for 30m. Notified on-call.

liam: Quick debug I ran locally: instrumented decrement paths and saw several code paths where we increment pinned_by=tool-output and on error/early-exit we don't decref. Sample log: 

```
DEBUG kv: pin_page id=0x7f9b2a8c by tool-output session=abcd
WARN toolchain: exception in tool X, propagating
# missing: kv: unpin_page id=0x7f9b2a8c
```

That would explain refcnts stuck at 2-3 forever.

maya: I opened PR #459 that adds explicit try/finally in the tool wrapper and logs an info every time a page is unpinned. Want people to run staging repro with that patch.

girish: Thanks — I'll run a canary tomorrow. Also propose an intermediate mitigation: change eviction scanner to consider "pinned_by_tool" with a TTL override — treat pins older than 5m as evictable (force-unpin-on-evict) unless explicitly marked sticky. This should keep long sessions from permanently anchoring pages.

hannah: Preliminary numbers from my local run: baseline (no fixes) RSS: 2.1G -> 2.6G after 2h. With force-unpin tweak RSS: 2.2G -> 2.25G (stable). So it looks promising.

maya: Good. Proposed next steps: 
- land PR #459 (safe try/finally in tool paths) 
- add unit test to cover tool exception/unwind unpin behavior 
- canary the eviction TTL tweak behind a flag and monitor per-session KV-page residency metric 
- add telemetry: histogram of page residency duration and pinned_by labels

liam: I'll pick up the unit test and add an assertion that refcnts drop to 0 after session tear-down.

girish: I'll prepare the canary flag and the TTL tweak, and we can A/B it on one canary shard.

perf-bot: Reminder: add a perf regression test for sequence-length distribution change (we should be able to simulate batch profile and ensure RAM delta < 100MB over 2h).

maya: Thanks all. If someone can run the patched build on staging tonight and paste pmap at 30/60/120m that'd be great. @girish @liam @hannah please coordinate. :thumbsup:

jonathan: I'll also add a short page to runbook describing how to use --kv-debug=pagewalk and what to look for (stuck refcnts, pinned_by metadata).
